An after-set with zero failures admits no added failure whatever the baseline held, so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids is empty; the baseline field is absent rather than measured, which is recorded here so the zero is not read as a measured baseline comparison.

findings.summary: In the readiness predicate _owner_ready, _select_engine's second return value is discarded (`selected, _ = ...`), so a request that arrived before its engine was in the catalog and was admitted when the engine appeared records routing null on its row even though _select_engine has just created or followed a pin for its key. The goal states every request row records pinned, placed or failed-over; this path is the one place the column is silently empty on an admitted generation request. It also skips the failover bound, because the bound is armed only when routing == 'pinned' at the main selection site (router.py:2440), so such a request waits the gate's full 300 s at its pinned engine rather than the 30 s bound.

The failover arm re-acquires at the alternate engine and then reports only the second admission's gate_wait_s, so the time a pinned request already spent queueing at its own engine (up to the 30 s bound) is dropped from the row: a request that waited 30 s and then failed over reports a near-zero gate wait, and the engine it actually waited at is not named in gate_engine. The re-acquisition at router.py:2488 has the same shape for the unbound-owner path, so this follows an existing pattern in the file rather than introducing a new one, but the failover path is new and its wait is now the one the pin exists to bound.

When every candidate engine's gate is paused, _rank_placement falls back to `pool = unpaused or live` (router.py:2173), so it can return the engine the key is already pinned to. _select_engine then returns that same engine with the string 'failed-over', and rewrites the pin to it: the row claims a move that did not happen, and a reader summing failed-over rows counts a failover that never occurred. The plan's rule is that placement skips engines whose gate is paused; the all-paused fallback is a deliberate departure but its label should be 'pinned' when the chosen engine is the pinned one.

Two departures the goal names have no test: loss of the engine (the pin's engine leaving the catalog, router.py:2205-2210, reached only when by_engine has no entry for the pinned id -- untested, though the pause arm covers the same code path's alternate branch), and the session-key fallback chain. Every test passes x-reckon-session, so _session_key's run-id and caller-host branches (router.py:2077-2083) are unexercised; a regression there, such as returning the host key always, would leave the suite green while sessions scattered with no pin at all.
